name: open the pull request and post the plan on it
about: Push the branch and open the PR with a description of the change. Then comment the plan onto it, with this step's `command` as it stands — that ONE plan and never the store, posted as the markdown it gives you, no fenced block, no summarising, no reformatting. It renders the plan AS IT STANDS AT THAT MOMENT — open steps, empty `output` fields and all — and waits for nothing: no step has to be finished first, and `merge` re-runs this same command later and edits the comment in place. So a definition telling you that some field of its own is what this comment dumps is saying why that field must be filled, never that the comment waits for it. The command is on the step so nobody has to reconstruct it; fill in the PR number and the plan id and run it. Obliges `change-approval`, which obliges `review`, so naming this step lands THREE steps in one act — and each lands where it runs rather than where it was named: change approval is an early root before the implementation, review comes after it, and this step waits on the review. Nothing about those deps needs fixing afterwards, provided the implementation is already in the plan when you name this: a step is placed against the plan as it stands, and nothing already in it is re-deped. WHAT IT REQUIRES, read from the change record rather than rerun: a CURRENT verification (`verification`, naming the commit it covers) and a RESOLVED review (`review`, no unresolved major) — the evidence is already there, so this reads it by identity and does not run it again. A DIRECT change reaches its PR here too, without any of the steps above: it has no plan, so there is no `change-approval` to oblige and no library step to name — its record is posted with this same `sb plugin plans comment <record> --pr <PR>`, and the record is what carries the human request, the verification and the review onto the pull request.
